tutorial.title: Customizing API Calls
tutorial.descriptionContent: Customize API calls to receive exactly what you ask for

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's explore how to make use of headers and the body in API requests to send data securely and customize the behavior of the requests.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
APIs often require authentication details to be sent through API headers. We can specify these headers while making the API request.

Make sure to pick headers, followed by headers, and finally headers.
lessons.hardModeContent:
APIs often require authentication details in headers. You can specify these headers while making the API request.

Store the API key in auth_headers and attach that dictionary as headers on the request.

Make sure to pick auth_headers, followed by headers, and finally auth_headers.

lessons.title: Lesson #2 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Headers in an API request are typically defined as a dictionary, with each key representing the header name.

Make sure to pick { followed by "api-key" and then :, "MY_SECRET_KEY", }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You typically define request headers as a dictionary, with each key naming a header.

Build the headers dictionary so api-key maps to MY_SECRET_KEY.

Make sure to pick {, followed by "api-key", :, "MY_SECRET_KEY", and finally }.

lessons.title: Lesson #2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can directly pass the dictionary to the headers parameter without saving it in a variable first.

However, for readability, it's best to define headers separately, particularly if they are complex or reused across multiple requests.

Make sure to pick "api-key", followed by "MY_SECRET_KEY".
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can pass the dictionary directly to the headers parameter without saving it in a variable first.

For readability, define headers separately, especially when they are complex or reused across multiple requests.

For this one request, pass MY_SECRET_KEY under api-key without creating a separate variable.

Make sure to pick headers, followed by "api-key", and finally "MY_SECRET_KEY".

lessons.title: Lesson #2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
To access an API requiring authentication, include the credentials in the headers, or access will be denied.

In the header, we typically add authentication information, such as API keys, tokens, or other metadata needed for the request.

Make sure to pick "api-key", followed by "MY_SECRET_KEY".
lessons.hardModeContent:
To access an API requiring authentication, include the credentials in the headers, or access will be denied.

In the header, you typically add authentication information, such as API keys or tokens needed for the request.

The API expects MY_SECRET_KEY in the api-key header. Fix the denied request.

Make sure to pick "api-key", followed by "MY_SECRET_KEY", and finally headers=headers.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Some APIs require data to be sent in the body of the request in addition to headers. We append it as json to the API call.

In the body, we typically add the data, such as user input, JSON objects, or other content to be sent to the server.

Make sure to pick body, followed by body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Some APIs need data in the request body as well as headers. You append the body as json to the API call.

In the body, you typically add user input, JSON objects, or other data to send to the server.

Send I was here! as JSON under my-message, keeping the API key in the headers.

Make sure to pick "my-message", followed by "I was here!", and finally json=payload.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Adding the header and body is part of forming the API request.

Depending on the endpoint, we must provide these to ensure the server understands and processes our request.

Make sure to pick headers followed by body and then headers, body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Adding the header and body is part of forming the API request.

Depending on the endpoint, you must provide these so the server can understand and process your request.

Complete the request so the API key is sent as a header and the message is sent as JSON.

Put the headers argument before the json argument.

Make sure to pick "api-key", followed by "my-message", headers=headers, and finally json=body.

lessons.title: Lesson #2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a headers dictionary and use it when making the API call.

Make sure to pick headers followed by = and then {"api-key": "MY_SECRET_KEY"}, headers, =, headers.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create a headers dictionary and use it when making the API call.

Store the key in auth_headers, request the user information, and save the response.

Make sure to pick auth_headers, followed by {"api-key": "MY_SECRET_KEY"}, response, requests.get, headers, and finally auth_headers.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a body dictionary and use it when making the API call.

Make sure to pick body followed by = and then {"my-message": "I was here!"}, json, =, body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create a body dictionary and use it when making the API call.

Send I was here! as JSON in a POST request, attaching the existing API-key headers.

Make sure to pick body, followed by {"my-message": "I was here!"}, requests.post, headers=headers, json, and finally body.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Where do you include an API key in an HTTP request using the requests library?

You include it in the headers parameterYou include it in the body parameter

You include it in the headers parameter.
lessons.hardModeContent:
With the requests library, we include an API key in the headers parameter.

The API key is stored in credentials. Which argument attaches it to a request?

headers=credentialsjson=credentialsparams=credentials

Make sure to pick headers=credentials.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
When making a POST request, where should the data, such as user details, be included?

It should be included in the body It should be included in the headers

It should be included in the body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When making a POST request, data such as user details belongs in the request body.

A signup request sends an API key and a new user's profile. Where should the profile go?

In the bodyIn the headers with the API keyIn the endpoint path

Make sure to pick In the body.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Query parameters are key-value pairs added to a URL to send additional data to the server, often used for filtering, sorting, etc.


They are part of the URL and specify filters or options, while headers and the body carry metadata and data.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
To add query parameters to the URL, you write a question mark ? followed by the query parameter.

Make sure to pick ?.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To add query parameters to the URL, you write a question mark ? followed by the query parameter.

You write each query parameter as key=value. Use popularity=high for this filter.

Complete the URL so it requests languages with high popularity.

Make sure to pick ?popularity=high.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
After the ?, we specify the key, an equals sign =, and the value.

Make sure to pick popularity, followed by =, and finally high.
lessons.hardModeContent:
After the ?, you specify the key, an equals sign =, and the value.

Filter languages by a popularity value of high.

Make sure to pick popularity, followed by =, and finally high.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also chain multiple query parameters together by separating them with an &.

Make sure to pick &.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can chain multiple query parameters by separating them with an &.

Keep the popularity filter and add limit with a value of 1.

Make sure to pick &limit=1.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Adding query parameters is tedious. Luckily, we can define them as a dictionary as well.

A dictionary like this is much simpler to read and maintain.

Make sure to pick { followed by "popularity": "high", and then "limit": 1, }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Adding query parameters to a URL can be tedious. You can define them as a dictionary instead.

A dictionary like this is much simpler to read and maintain.

Create params for high popularity and a numeric limit of 1.

Make sure to pick params, followed by {, "popularity": "high",, "limit": 1, and finally }.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can pass the dictionary with the query parameters as params to requests.get.

This ensures the URL is properly formatted and makes the code cleaner and easier to maintain.

Make sure to pick params, followed by params, and finally params.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can pass the query-parameter dictionary as params to requests.get.

This ensures the URL is properly formatted and makes the code cleaner and easier to maintain.

Attach filters so the GET request returns one highly popular language.

Make sure to pick filters, followed by params, and finally filters.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Lastly, let's work with pagination through query parameters. Pagination limits the amount of data returned for better readability.

Make sure to pick "page":, followed by 3.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can use pagination query parameters to limit how much data a request returns.

Request page 3 using page with a numeric value, then attach the query parameters.

Make sure to pick "page": 3, followed by params=params.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
Where are query parameters included in an HTTP request?

They are appended to the URL after a ? symbolThey are included in the headers of the request

They are appended to the URL after a ? symbol.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Query parameters are appended to the URL after a ? symbol.

Which URL requests exercises whose type is python?

/exercises?type=python/exercises&type=python/exercises/type=python

Make sure to pick /exercises?type=python.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
How are multiple query parameters added to a URL?

They are separated by & symbols in the URL They are separated by commas in the URL

They are separated by & symbols in the URL.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Multiple query parameters are separated by & symbols in the URL.

Which URL requests highly popular languages with a limit of 1?

/languages?popularity=high&limit=1/languages?popularity=high,limit=1/languages?popularity=high?limit=1

/languages?popularity=high&limit=1.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the URL by setting the query parameter popularity.

Make sure to pick ? followed by popularity and then =, high.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the URL by setting the query parameter popularity.

Combine the base URL and filter key so the completed URL requests high popularity.

Make sure to pick base_url, followed by "?", filter_key, and finally "=high".

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the code by setting headers, params, and data correctly.

Make sure to pick headers followed by params and then data, headers, params, data.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use api-key for authentication, search for python, and name for John.

Send the headers first, query parameters second, and JSON body last.

Make sure to pick "api-key", followed by "search", "name", headers=headers, params=params, and finally json=data.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the URL.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by &.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the URL so it requests highly popular languages and limits the result to 1.

Make sure to pick ?popularity=high, followed by &limit=1.
